svg.title: One provider-neutral core, two ways to adopt it
svg.desc: The abstract fleet-architecture path and the prescriptive fleet-preset path share a provider-neutral core of functions, protocols, an autonomy layer and primitives. Cross-provider translation is a plan from a primitive map with unverified targets, not an implemented compiler.
svg.text: One provider-neutral core, two ways to adopt it
Neither path grants authority or activates anything; installation and activation stay explicit.
Feedback loops with measured, reversible change
Pure functions; no domain roles prescribed
Domains plug into the reviewer function
Tunable parameters (round cap, waivers) are yours
Truthfulness and authority constraints always apply
Named domain seats, each bound to one function
Strict defaults: exact-head PASS, clean automated
review, no on-merge running, net script delta ≤ 0
Relaxations are recorded opt-ins, never defaults
Other providers: a plan, not a compiler
Primitive map → target bindings (Grok Bot is the source; other targets are unverified TODOs)
→ conformance replay before anything is emitted. Skill install is the only non-Grok binding marked supported.
